sentences.text: 8 26-02-2026 I.A. No. 01 of 2026 Heard the learned counsel for the appellant as well as the informant and the learned APP for the State.

2. The appellant has preferred the present appeal in this Hon'ble Court against the judgment and order dated 17.10.2023 passed by the learned Exclusive Special Judge (POCSO Act), Darbhanga in POCSO G.R. Case No. 44 of 2020 arising out of Kamtaul P.S. Case No. 208 of 2020 whereby and whereunder the appellant was convicted for the offence under Sections 376, 506 of the IPC and Section 4(i) of the POCSO Act Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.5677 of 2023(8) dt.26-02-2026 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs. 10,000/- and in default S.I. for six months under Section 376 of the IPC.
He was also sentenced to undergo imprisonment of two years and fine of Rs. 3,000/- and in default S.I. for one month under Section 406 of the IPC.

sentences.text: He, however, was pleased to order that in view of Section 42 of the POCSO Act, the convict will undergo R.I. for a term of 10 years with fine of Rs. 10,000/- only and in default S.I. for six months for the offence under Section 376 of the IPC and Section 4(i) of the POCSO Act.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the appellant is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in this case.
No occurrence as alleged by the prosecution has taken place.
The appellant is in custody since 19.08.2020 and thus, he has completed five years six months in custody which is half of the sentence awarded to the appellant.

4. Learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submits that in the present case, allegedly, while the informant went to the house of the accused in a marriage ceremony, the accused (appellant) ravished her on the Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.5677 of 2023(8)
dt.26-02-2026 false pretext of marriage and also took nude photographs of the victim.
It is a heinous crime where a minor girl was raped by the appellant on the false pretext of marriage.
5. Having considered the rival submissions of the parties, I am of the view that the appellant does not deserve privilege of bail.

Accordingly, his prayer for bail is rejected and consequently, I.A. No. 01 of 2026 also stands rejected.
6.

However, considering the fact that the appellant is in languishing in custody for five and a half years, let this appeal be listed on 06.04.2026 under the heading 'For Hearing'.
7.

It is made clear that if the appeal is not taken up for final hearing within a period of three months,
the appellant will be at liberty to renew his prayer.

(Nawneet Kumar Pandey, J) priyanka/-
